newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Dec official reserves 300.22 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: French Dec official reserves 300.22 bln Ffr.

text.p: The Bank of France and finance ministry gave the following breakdown of offical gold and foreign exchange reserves (in billions of francs)
Note - The accounting basis has changed.

A joint Bank of France/finance ministry statement said that the gold reserves figure fell due to the use of a new reference rate for gold, the 1997 first quarter reference rate of 62,626 franc per kilo, instead of 64,706 francs previously.
The new rate was based on the daily gold rate in London during the last quarter of 1996 converted into francs on the basis of the daily dollar rate in Paris for the same period.

Foreign exchange reserves rose partly due to transactions in the month of December and partly due to their being based on the exchange rates in Paris on December 27. Those rates were 5.2530 francs per dollar and 3.3727 francs per mark.
That compared to 5.1745 and 3.3832 respectively last time.
Ecu reserves rose partly due to a change to 6.55867 francs per Ecu from 6.48048 in the second half of 1996.
Credits with the IMF rose too, partly because the SDR (Special Drawing Rate) was reevaluated at 7.53060 against the franc for the first half of 1997 versus 7.43681 in the second half of 1996.
